description: The image displays three pie charts comparing four categories across three difficulty levels labeled "easy," "medium," and "hard," with a general label "Zero-Shot" centered below the medium chart. Each of the three pie charts contains four slices. A single legend on the right side identifies the categories by color, and exact percentage labels are positioned directly inside the corresponding slices of each chart. None of the slices are visually emphasized, exploded, or offset. In the "easy" chart, the largest slice is teal (N+K+) at 55.4%, followed by yellow (N−K+) at 38.3%, orange (N−K−) at 4.6%, and red (N+K−) at 1.7%, with the segments ordered clockwise in descending size. The "medium" chart shows a similar visual arrangement, with the teal slice (N+K+) at 58.8%, the yellow slice (N−K+) at 35.4%, the orange slice (N−K−) at 4.0%, and the red slice (N+K−) at 1.8%. The "hard" chart presents a different distribution where the orange slice (N−K−) is the largest at 37.9%, closely followed by the yellow slice (N−K+) at 37.3%, the teal slice (N+K+) at 18.1%, and the red slice (N+K−) at 6.7%.
